content: Magnesium hydroxide, when administered at a concentration of 400 mg/5 mL, should be taken orally in doses of 30-60 mL per day, either at bedtime or divided into multiple doses throughout the day. For a higher concentration of 800 mg/5 mL, the recommended dosage is 15-30 mL per day, also taken orally at bedtime or in divided doses. Chewable tablets can be taken up to 8 tablets per day, either at bedtime or in divided doses. For acute dosing, magnesium hydroxide (400 mg/5 mL) can be administered orally in doses of 5-15 mL every 4 hours, but no more than 4 doses should be taken within a 24-hour period. Similarly, chewable tablets can be taken in doses of 2-4 tablets every 4 hours, with a maximum of 4 doses in 24 hours. The safety and efficacy of magnesium hydroxide in children under 2 years of age have not been established. Magnesium hydroxide interacts with several medications by altering their absorption or bioavailability, primarily through cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract or by increasing gastric pH. These interactions can lead to reduced plasma levels and therapeutic effects of the co-administered drugs. Below are detailed interactions: 1. Baloxavir marboxil: Magnesium hydroxide decreases the absorption of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Studies in monkeys have shown significant reductions in plasma levels when co-administered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. No human studies have been conducted. 2. Demeclocycline, doxycycline, minocycline, oxytetracycline, tetracycline, omadacycline, sarecycline: Magnesium hydroxide inhibits the GI absorption of these tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or separate dosing by several hours. 3. Eltrombopag: Magnesium hydroxide reduces eltrombopag levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Co-administration is contraindicated. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. 4. Infigratinib: Magnesium hydroxide decreases infigratinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. If co-administration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer infigratinib 2 hours before and after magnesium hydroxide. 5. Pazopanib, ponatinib, crizotinib, vismodegib: Magnesium hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing the solubility and bioavailability of these drugs. Avoid co-administration or use short-acting antacids instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, separating doses by several hours. 6. Raltegavir, dolutegravir, bictegravir, cabotegravir: Magnesium hydroxide reduces the plasma levels of these integrase inhibitors by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer these drugs 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium hydroxide. 7. Ciprofloxacin, gemifloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, ofloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide inhibits the GI absorption of these fluoroquinolones, reducing their bioavailability. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium hydroxide. 8. Chloroquine: Magnesium hydroxide reduces chloroquine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 9. Penicillamine: Magnesium hydroxide inhibits the GI absorption of penicillamine. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 10. Pexidartinib: Magnesium hydroxide reduces pexidartinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours before or after magnesium hydroxide. 11. Riociguat: Magnesium hydroxide reduces riociguat levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by at least 1 hour. 12. Ibandronate: Magnesium hydroxide reduces ibandronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or separate doses. 13. Nitrofurantoin: Magnesium hydroxide reduces nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or separate doses. 14. Pancrelipase: Magnesium hydroxide may antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of pancrelipase. Use with caution and monitor closely. 15. Vitamin D: Vitamin D increases serum magnesium levels, particularly in patients with renal impairment. Avoid combined use in patients with chronic renal failure. 16. Amiloride, spironolactone, triamterene: These drugs increase magnesium levels by reducing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. 17. Amikacin, gentamicin, tobramycin, streptomycin, neomycin: These aminoglycosides decrease magnesium levels by increasing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. 18. Loop diuretics (e.g., furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide), thiazide diuretics (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide, chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, indapamide, metolazone): These diuretics decrease magnesium levels by increasing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. 19. Estrogens (e.g., estradiol, conjugated estrogens, esterified estrogens): Estrogens may shift magnesium from blood to tissue storage, reducing serum magnesium levels. Use with caution and monitor closely. 20. Sodium polystyrene sulfonate: This drug increases magnesium levels by reducing renal clearance, with a potential risk of alkalosis. Use with caution and monitor closely. 21. Calcitonin salmon: This drug increases magnesium levels by reducing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. 22. Doxercalciferol: This drug increases magnesium levels by enhancing GI absorption. Use with caution and monitor closely. 23. Mestranol: Mestranol may shift magnesium from blood to tissue storage, reducing serum magnesium levels. Use with caution and monitor closely. 24. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens: This combination may shift magnesium from blood to tissue storage, reducing serum magnesium levels. Use with caution and monitor closely. 25. Ethacrynic acid, mannitol: These drugs decrease magnesium levels by increasing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. In summary, magnesium hydroxide interacts with a wide range of medications, primarily by altering their absorption or bioavailability through cation binding or changes in gastric pH. These interactions necessitate careful consideration of dosing intervals, alternative therapies, or close monitoring to ensure therapeutic efficacy and patient safety.
